mainTopic: How ארץ ישראל was divided among the שבטים: equal portions per שבט, money payments to even out land values, and the use of a גורל together with the אורים ותומים.
overview: The גמרא wants to prove that ארץ ישראל was divided by שבטים. It brings the פסוק 'בין רב למעט' and then a long ברייתא. The ברייתא says the first division was among twelve שבטים and the future one will be among thirteen. It says money was used to even out the value of the portions, and that a גורל and the אורים ותומים worked together: אלעזר announced the result, and the lottery boxes confirmed it. It also says that in the future everyone will get every kind of land, and הקדוש ברוך הוא will divide it Himself. From the line 'twelve שבטים' the גמרא concludes that the land was divided by שבטים. The גמרא then explains parts of the ברייתא. The thirteenth share is real land for the נשיא. The money made up for land that was near or far from ירושלים, and תנאים argue whether that was paid in money or in land. Finally, 'אך בגורל' teaches that יהושע and כלב got their land by the word of ה׳ and not by lottery. The proof for יהושע is brought here, and the proof for כלב comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A proof from the verse 'between the more and the fewer'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק 'בין רב למעט' to show how the land was divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a proof: the פסוק says 'between the more and the fewer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק as a proof for the question it is dealing with: was the land divided by שבטים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the inheritance is divided 'between the more and the fewer.' This suggests that a large שבט and a small שבט each got a similar share as a whole. That means each person got a different amount depending on how big his שבט was. So the division was done by שבט, not by head count.

keyTerms.meaning: Between the more and the fewer (במדבר 26:56)

phrases.english: Come and hear a proof:
"Between the more and the fewer."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier question (before this section) about how the land was divided.
steps.raayaObject: The land was divided equally among the שבטים, not by individual heads.

steps.title: A ברייתא: twelve שבטים then, thirteen in the future
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a second proof. It opens by saying the future division will be among thirteen שבטים, while the first division was among twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, a ברייתא teaches: ארץ ישראל will one day be divided among thirteen שבטים. At first it was divided only among twelve שבטים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second proof from a ברייתא, which begins by comparing the future division with the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא counts the division by שבטים: twelve in the past and thirteen in the future. Speaking in terms of שבטים fits the idea that the land is split up by שבט. The first division had only twelve because שבט לוי got no portion of land.

keyTerms.meaning: Is going to, in the future

phrases.english: And also, it was taught in a ברייתא:
Eretz Yisrael is destined
to be divided among thirteen tribes,
for at first it was divided
only among twelve tribes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, supporting proof to the פסוק brought in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The land was divided by שבטים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about how the land was divided, then and in the future.

steps.title: Land values were evened out with money
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the division was balanced with money, based on 'בין רב למעט.' רבי יהודה shows how different land values can be.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was divided only with money, as it says 'between the more and the fewer.' רבי יהודה said: a סאה of land in יהודה is worth five סאה of land in the גליל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues: money payments between the שבטים were used to even out differences in the value of their portions, so that every share came out fair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the same פסוק, 'בין רב למעט', is read as being about value: portions worth more and portions worth less were evened out with money. רבי יהודה shows how big value gaps can be. Land that grows one סאה in יהודה is worth as much as land that grows five סאה in the גליל. Step 18 explains what difference the money actually covered.

keyTerms.meaning: With money: payments to even out values
A measure of grain; here, the land needed to grow one סאה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 1. There, 'בין רב למעט' was about big and small שבטים. Here the ברייתא uses the same פסוק for evening out land values with money.

phrases.english: And it was divided only with money,
as it is stated: "Between the more and the fewer."
Rabbi Yehuda said:
A se'a in Judea
is worth five se'a in the Galilee.
phrases.notes: He means the land that grows that much grain, not the grain itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second detail about the division.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Differences in land value between portions were evened out with money payments. Land values could differ by as much as five to one.

steps.title: Divided by lottery and by the אורים ותומים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings two פסוקים: one shows the land was divided by a גורל, and the other shows it was divided by the אורים ותומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was divided only by lottery, as it says 'only by lot.' And it was divided only by the אורים ותומים, as it says 'by the mouth of the lot.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists two more ways the land was divided, each with its own פסוק. This sets up a question, because the two seem to point in different directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אך בגורל' tells us a lottery was used. The ברייתא reads 'על פי הגורל' (by the mouth of the lot) as speaking, which hints at the אורים ותומים. Both are said with 'only' (לא... אלא), so the obvious question is how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy breastplate the כהן גדול wore, through which answers were given

phrases.english: And it was divided only by lottery,
as it is stated: "Only by lot."
And it was divided only with the Urim VeTummim,
as it is stated: "By the pronouncement of the lot."
phrases.notes: במדבר 26:56. Literally 'by the mouth of the lot'; a lot that 'speaks' points to the אורים ותומים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with two more methods of division.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The division was done both by a גורל and by the אורים ותומים, each learned from a פסוק.

steps.title: How can both methods be true?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how the land could be divided both by a lottery and by the אורים ותומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did this work?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how the two פסוקים from step 4 fit together. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק seems to say that only one method was used. The question asks for a picture of the process in which both the lottery and the אורים ותומים played a part.

keyTerms.meaning: How is this? How do these fit together?

phrases.english: How so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the two methods listed in step 4 can both be true.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the lottery and the אורים ותומים worked together in the division.

steps.title: The scene: אלעזר with the אורים ותומים and two lottery boxes
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins its answer by describing the setup: אלעזר wears the אורים ותומים, everyone stands before him, and two lottery boxes are placed in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אלעזר was dressed in the אורים ותומים, and יהושע and all of ישראל stood before him. A box of the שבטים and a box of the borders were placed before him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts to answer by setting the scene. Steps 7 and 8 finish the answer by showing what אלעזר did with the two boxes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two boxes: one holds the names of the שבטים, and the other holds the borders of the land's regions. אלעזר wearing the אורים ותומים shows that both methods are being joined together. How they work together will be explained right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: A box or urn used for drawing lots
Borders, the regions of the land

phrases.english: Elazar was dressed in the Urim VeTummim,
and Joshua and all of Israel
were standing before him;
and a lottery box of the tribes
and a lottery box of the boundaries
were placed before him;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 5 by describing the setup.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer so far is only the setup: אלעזר wearing the אורים ותומים, with two lottery boxes (one for the שבטים, one for the borders) in front of him. Steps 7 and 8 complete it.

steps.title: אלעזר announces זבולן and עכו, and the lottery confirms it
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר announces through רוח הקודש that זבולן and the region of עכו will come up, and then both lottery boxes produce exactly that.
steps.simpleTranslation: אלעזר would focus with רוח הקודש and say: 'זבולן is coming up, and the region of עכו is coming up with it.' He mixed the box of שבטים and זבולן came up. He mixed the box of regions and the region of עכו came up.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its answer from Step 6. It shows how the אורים ותומים and the גורל worked together: first a prediction, then the lottery matching it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 asked how the land could be divided both by a lottery and by the אורים ותומים. Here we see that both happened at once. אלעזר announced the result ahead of time with divine help, and the lottery then confirmed it publicly.

keyTerms.meaning: Focuses, aims to know (here: figures out the result)
Mixed or shook (the lots in the box)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the order: the announcement comes first and the drawing comes after. The lottery is not deciding something new. It confirms what was already announced, and that is how one process is both a גורל and אורים ותומים.

phrases.english: And he would focus with the Divine Spirit and say:
Zevulun is coming up,
the region of Akko is coming up with it.
He mixed the lots in the box of the tribes,
and Zevulun came up in his hand.
He mixed the lots in the box of the regions,
and the region of Akko came up in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer begun in Step 6 by describing what אלעזר actually did with the two boxes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How could the land be divided both by גורל and by אורים ותומים (Step 5)?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אלעזר announced the result through רוח הקודש, and then the lottery confirmed it.

steps.title: The same process repeats for נפתלי and every other שבט
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר does the same for נפתלי and the region of גינוסר, and then for every שבט.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would focus again with רוח הקודש and say: 'נפתלי is coming up, and the region of גינוסר is coming up with it.' He mixed the box of שבטים and נפתלי came up. He mixed the box of regions and גינוסר came up. And so it went for every single שבט.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second example and then says the same thing happened for every שבט. This finishes the answer to the question in Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second example shows the process was a fixed method that repeated, not a one-time event. The phrase וְכֵן כׇּל שֵׁבֶט וָשֵׁבֶט tells us every שבט got its portion this way, as a שבט.

keyTerms.meaning: Ginosar, a region by the Kinneret
And so for every single tribe

steps.whatToRemember: The division used both methods together: אלעזר predicted through the אורים ותומים, and the גורל confirmed it, one שבט at a time.

phrases.english: And he would again focus with the Divine Spirit and say:
Naftali is coming up,
and the region of Ginosar is coming up with it.
He mixed the lots in the box of the tribes,
and Naftali came up in his hand.
He mixed the lots in the box of the regions,
and the region of Ginosar came up in his hand.
And so with each and every tribe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the method of Step 7 with a second שבט and applies it to all the שבטים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How could the land be divided both by גורל and by אורים ותומים (Step 5)?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The same predict-then-draw process was used for every שבט.

steps.title: In the future, everyone will get every kind of land
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא contrasts the two divisions. Today a person has either grain land or orchard land, but in עולם הבא everyone will have land in the mountain, the lowland and the valley.
steps.simpleTranslation: The division of עולם הבא will not be like the division of this world. In this world, a person who has a grain field has no orchard, and one who has an orchard has no grain field. In עולם הבא, there is no one who will not have land in the mountain, the lowland and the valley, as it says (יחזקאל): 'The gate of ראובן, one; the gate of יהודה, one; the gate of לוי, one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a new point, the future division of the land, and explains how it will be different from the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first division each portion came from one kind of land, so a person did not have every type of field. In the future, every portion will include every type of land. The פסוק from יחזקאל, which gives each שבט one equal gate, supports the idea that portions will be equal.

keyTerms.meaning: The World to Come (here, the future era)
A grain field (literally 'white field'), with no trees
Mountain, lowland, valley: the three kinds of terrain

phrases.english: And not like the division of this world
is the division of the World to Come.

phrases.aramaic: הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, אָדָם יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׂדֵה לָבָן –
phrases.english: In this world, if a person has a grain field,
he has no orchard field;

phrases.aramaic: שְׂדֵה פַרְדֵּס – אֵין לוֹ שְׂדֵה לָבָן.
phrases.english: if he has an orchard field, he has no grain field.

phrases.aramaic: לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, אֵין לָךְ כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
phrases.english: In the World to Come, you will not find anyone
who does not have land in the mountain, the lowland, and the valley,
as it says: 'The gate of Reuven, one;

phrases.aramaic: שַׁעַר יְהוּדָה אֶחָד, שַׁעַר לֵוִי אֶחָד״.
phrases.english: the gate of Yehuda, one; the gate of Levi, one.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא כַּחֲלוּקָּה שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה חֲלוּקָּה שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the description of the first division, the ברייתא contrasts it with the future one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future division, every person will get land of every kind of terrain.

steps.title: God Himself will divide the land in the future
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that הקדוש ברוך הוא will divide the future portions Himself, based on a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא divides it for them Himself, as it says: 'And these are their portions, says ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the ברייתא. It adds one more difference: in the future, no lottery or כהן will be needed, because God Himself will divide the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first division went through אלעזר, the אורים ותומים and the גורל. The future division will be done directly by הקדוש ברוך הוא. The proof is the words 'נאם ה׳' attached to 'their portions.'

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְחַלֵּק לָהֶן בְּעַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, divides it for them Himself,
as it says: 'And these are their portions, says the Lord.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְחַלֵּק לָהֶן בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final difference between the future division and the first one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will personally divide the land.

steps.title: Proof: the land was divided by tribes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's opening line, 'the first time it was divided only among twelve שבטים,' and concludes that the land was divided by שבטים. It confirms this.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches: 'The first time, it was divided only among twelve שבטים.' Learn from this that it was divided by שבטים! Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the long ברייתא is finished, the גמרא points to the one line it needed. That line proves the land was divided by שבטים, and the גמרא agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מִיהַת ('in any case') tells us that most of the ברייתא doesn't matter for this proof. Only its opening line, from Step 2, matters. Since it describes the first division as being 'among twelve שבטים,' the land was divided by שבטים and not head by head.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches (points to the key line)
Learn from this (said once as a proof, then again to confirm it)

steps.whatToRemember: The final takeaway is that ארץ ישראל was divided by שבטים. The proof comes from the ברייתא's opening words, not from its details about the lottery or the future.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the proof in the long story about the boxes or עולם הבא. The גמרא uses only the opening line of the ברייתא from Step 2.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles which way the land was split up in this sugya: by שבטים.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: ״שֶׁבַּתְּחִלָּה לֹא נִתְחַלְּקָה אֶלָּא לִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים״;
phrases.english: 'For at first it was divided only among twelve tribes';
phrases.notes: This is the opening line of the ברייתא, back in Step 2.

phrases.english: Learn from this that it was divided by tribes!
Yes, learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the ברייתא's details to its opening line in order to finish the proof begun in Step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That ארץ ישראל was divided by שבטים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's words 'שבתחלה לא נתחלקה אלא לשנים עשר שבטים'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The land was divided by שבטים, and the גמרא confirms this with 'שמע מינה.'

steps.title: Who gets the thirteenth portion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that in the future the land will be split into thirteen shares and asks who gets the extra share.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: The Land of Israel will one day be divided into thirteen shares. There are only twelve שבטים, so who gets the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a line of the ברייתא about the future division and asks a simple question. Since there are only twelve שבטים, who gets the thirteenth share? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the future division will have thirteen shares. Twelve are obviously for the twelve שבטים. The extra one needs an owner, so the גמרא asks who it is.

keyTerms.meaning: destined to / will in the future

phrases.english: The Master said:
The Land of Israel is destined to be divided
among thirteen tribes.
The other one, for whom is it?
phrases.notes: Twelve shares go to the twelve שבטים, so who gets the thirteenth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to another line of the ברייתא after the conclusion about dividing by שבטים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who receives the thirteenth portion in the future division?

steps.title: רב חסדא: the extra share is for the king
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the thirteenth share belongs to the נשיא (the king), and he proves it from a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is for the king. The פסוק says, 'And those who serve the city, from all the tribes of Israel, shall work it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question from the last step. The thirteenth share goes to the נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about someone who 'serves the city' and is supported by all the שבטים together. רב חסדא reads this as the king, who works for the whole nation, so the nation gives him a portion.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: For the king,
as it is written: "And those who serve the city
from all the tribes of Israel shall work it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The thirteenth portion is for the נשיא, based on יחזקאל 48:19.

steps.title: Maybe the king just gets wages
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי: maybe the פסוק only means the king gets paid by the people, not that he gets land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Maybe the פסוק just means plain wages!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on the proof. Maybe 'all the tribes serve him' only means they pay the king, and he does not get his own piece of land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 13 depends on reading the פסוק as talking about land. רב פפא offers another reading: the king is supported by payments. If that reading is right, the פסוק does not prove there is a thirteenth land portion.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Say it means mere wages!
phrases.notes: He means the people might just pay the king, like a salary or taxes, with no land at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי, אֵימָא רוּנְגָּר בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof פסוק used in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's reading of יחזקאל 48:19 as referring to land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could mean the king is supported by wages, not given a portion of land.

steps.title: A second פסוק shows it is real land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the wages idea. Another פסוק says the remaining land on both sides of the holy area goes to the נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that. The פסוק says: 'And what is left shall be for the prince, on this side and on that side of the holy portion and of the city's holding.'
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered. A later פסוק clearly talks about a real piece of land that belongs to the נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'on this side and on that side' describe a physical area of land, and a salary has no sides. So the king really does get land, and the thirteenth share is his.

keyTerms.meaning: the holy portion (area set aside as holy)

steps.whatToRemember: In the future division there are thirteen shares. The extra one is real land for the נשיא, not just wages.

phrases.english: That should not enter your mind,
as it is written: "And the remainder shall be for the prince
on this side and on that side
of the holy portion and of the city's holding."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Additional פסוק proves the portion is physical land.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The king might only receive wages.
steps.terutzMaskana: The נשיא receives an actual tract of land on both sides of the holy portion.

steps.title: Money was used in the division, but for what?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that the land was divided with money, and asks what the money was for.
steps.simpleTranslation: The land was divided only with money, as it says, 'Between the many and the few.' What was the money for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the ברייתא, which says money was part of the division. It asks what difference the money was making up. This sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money in a land division means some people paid others to make the shares fair. The question is which difference between the shares needed fixing.

keyTerms.meaning: between the many and the few

phrases.english: And it was divided only with money,
as it says: "Between the many and the few."
Regarding what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What difference between portions did the money compensate for?

steps.title: Not for good land versus bad land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the money made up for poor-quality land, because nobody sensible would trade good land for cash.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it was for nice land versus poor land, are we dealing with fools?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible answer and throws it out right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying someone to accept worse land assumes that person would agree to the trade. The גמרא says only a fool would take bad land for money. So the money must have been making up some other difference, which the next step names.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say...? (introduces a rhetorical rejection)

phrases.english: If you say it was for good land and poor land,
are we dealing with fools?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא לְשׁוּפְרָא וְסַנְיָא, אַטּוּ בְּשׁוּפְטָנֵי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects a first answer to step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that money compensated for land quality.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No sensible person would accept poor land in exchange for money.

steps.title: The money was for near versus far land
steps.stepSummary: The real answer is that money made up the difference between land close to ירושלים and land far from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was for land that is close and land that is far.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer. The money evened out location, near versus far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land near ירושלים is worth more because it is close to the city. Those who got near land paid the ones who got far land, so every share was fair.

phrases.english: Rather, for close land and far land.
phrases.notes: He means close to or far from ירושלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after step 17 rejected the first option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The money compensated for the difference between land near ירושלים and land far from it.

steps.title: A מחלוקת: even out with money or with land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes a תנאים dispute. רבי אליעזר says the difference was made up with money. רבי יהושע says it was made up with extra land.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of תנאים. רבי אליעזר says they evened it out with money. רבי יהושע says they evened it out with land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that תנאים argue over how the near and far shares were evened out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's statement that money was used fits רבי אליעזר. רבי יהושע holds the far shares were made bigger in land instead of being paid cash.

keyTerms.meaning: it is like a dispute of תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: Near land was worth more than far land, and the difference was evened out. רבי אליעזר says with money, רבי יהושע says with extra land.

phrases.english: It is like a dispute between Tannaim:
Rabbi Eliezer says: They evened it out with money.
phrases.notes: Literally 'they raised it', meaning they made up the difference.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: They evened it out with land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the compensation in step 18 is the subject of a תנאים dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: compensation in money. רבי יהושע: compensation in land.

steps.title: Divided by lottery, except for יהושע and כלב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the land was divided only by lottery, and a teaching adds that the word 'only' leaves out יהושע and כלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The land was divided only by lottery, as it says, 'Only by lot.' A ברייתא taught: 'Only by lot' leaves out יהושע and כלב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the ברייתא about the גורל. A teaching reads the word אך ('only') as excluding יהושע and כלב, and the next step asks what exactly that means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אך is often read as limiting a rule. Here it tells us that יהושע and כלב were not part of the regular lottery rule.

keyTerms.meaning: only (a word that limits or excludes)

phrases.english: And it was divided only by lottery,
as it says: "Only by lot."
It was taught: "Only by lot":
Joshua and Caleb are excluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The land was divided by גורל. The word אך excludes יהושע and כלב.

steps.title: They surely did get their own land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what way יהושע and כלב were excluded. It rejects the idea that they got no land, since they even took the מרגלים' shares.
steps.simpleTranslation: Excluded from what? If you say they took nothing at all, that can't be. They took shares that were not theirs, so of course they took their own!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'excluded' means and rules out the simplest guess.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned earlier in the מסכת (קיח ע"ב) that יהושע and כלב inherited the shares of the מרגלים. If they took other people's shares, they obviously took their own. So 'excluded' cannot mean they got nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'יצאו יהושע וכלב' as 'they got no land.' The גמרא proves they did get land. They just did not get it by the lottery.

phrases.english: Regarding what?
If you say that they did not take at all,
now, if what was not theirs they took,
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier teaching that they took the shares of the מרגלים.

phrases.english: is it even a question about their own?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the exclusion in step 20 means and rejects the first possibility.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that יהושע and כלב received no portion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They received even the מרגלים' portions, so they certainly received their own.

steps.title: They got land by God's word, not by lottery
steps.stepSummary: The exclusion means יהושע and כלב received their land by direct command of ה׳ and not through the lottery. A פסוק in ספר יהושע proves this for יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they did not take by lottery but by the word of ה׳. For יהושע, the פסוק says: 'By the word of ה׳ they gave him the city he asked for, תמנת סרח in the hill country of אפרים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real meaning of the exclusion and starts bringing proof, beginning with יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone else got land by lottery. יהושע and כלב got land that ה׳ specifically assigned to them. The פסוק says יהושע received the exact city he asked for, 'by the word of ה׳', not by drawing lots.
steps.whatToRemember: יהושע and כלב did get land, but they got it by God's direct command and not by the גורל.

phrases.english: Rather, that they did not take by lottery,
but by the word of God.
Joshua, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל פִּי ה׳ נָתְנוּ לוֹ אֶת הָעִיר אֲשֶׁר שָׁאָל,
phrases.english: "By the word of God they gave him the city that he asked for,
Timnat Serach in the hill country of Ephraim."
phrases.notes: יהושע 19:50. The proof for כלב comes next.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא נָטְלוּ בְּגוֹרָל, אֶלָּא עַל פִּי ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct meaning of the exclusion after step 21 rejected the first option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יהושע and כלב received portions by God's command rather than by lottery, as shown for יהושע in יהושע 19:50.
